pr.title: Consider parent predicates in ImpossiblePredicates pass.
pr.description:
This pass is double edged. It avoids some ICEs (yay!) but also degrades diagnostics from constant evaluation.

Fixes rust-lang/rust#121363
Fixes rust-lang/rust#131507
Fixes rust-lang/rust#140100 
Fixes rust-lang/rust#140365

analysis.summary: ImpossiblePredicates must consider the full predicate chain (including parent predicates) and must guard error-carrying and unevaluated-const-projection clauses. The old pass used only the body def's own global predicates, so bodies of nested/derived items under an impossible ancestor bound stayed reachable; later MIR optimization/const-eval then hit uncomputable layouts and ICE'd. The fix also deliberately clears error-referencing bodies, degrading const-eval diagnostics to "entering unreachable code".
analysis.originalLogic: ImpossiblePredicates ran on a MIR body and computed predicates as `tcx.predicates_of(body.source.def_id()).predicates.iter().filter_map(|(p, _)| if p.is_global() { Some(*p) } else { None })`, i.e. only the def's own predicates, filtered to global ones. It elaborated that sequence and, if `traits::impossible_predicates(tcx, ...)` was true, cleared the body to a single `unreachable` block (truncating basic blocks to 1).
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect transformation decided "this body is unreachable" from only the body's own global predicates, ignoring inherited parent predicates, and without screening out error-containing predicates or clauses with unevaluated constant projections. Thus a derived impl/closure/nested item whose enclosing item had an impossible where clause (e.g. `str: Sized`, `for<T> T: Copy`) was left as reachable, so later GVN/const-prop/const-eval tried to evaluate values whose layout was uncomputable and ICE'd (e.g. ScalarPair vs Scalar ABI). Conversely, passing error-carrying or const-projection predicates directly into the impossibility check could itself cause cycles/ICE. The corrected transformation uses `predicates_of(...).instantiate_identity(tcx)` (parent predicates included), filters with `!p.has_type_flags(TypeFlags::HAS_FREE_LOCAL_NAMES | TypeFlags::HAS_CT_PROJECTION)`, and clears the body when `predicates.references_error() || traits::impossible_predicates(...)`.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust functions, closures, and derived impl bodies whose own or inherited where-clauses contain impossible/trivial global predicates, and which perform const evaluation/promotion or layout-dependent operations. Examples from the patch/issues: a struct `TwoStrs(str, str) where str: Sized` with `#[derive(Debug)]` (derived impl inherits the parent bound); a function with `where for<T> T: Copy`; `fn a() where b: Sized` and `fn f() -> &'static str where Self: Sized` (error-type bounds); `fn foo() where (): Project` with `size_of::<<() as Project>::Assoc>()`; `where str: Pointee<Metadata = str>`; generic-const-expr type-alias bounds. Often requires `#![feature(trivial_bounds)]` / `non_lifetime_binders`, and optimization flags such as `-Zmir-enable-passes=+GVN -Zmir-enable-passes=+Inline -Zvalidate-mir`, `-C opt-level=1`, or `-Zmir-opt-level=5`.
analysis.trigger: A body is optimized/const-evaluated even though an enclosing item's where clause is globally unsatisfiable (or contains a type error), because the impossibility check inspected only the body's own predicates instead of the instantiated identity predicate set. Const promotion, array-length evaluation, or GVN simplification then produces an operand/layout inconsistent with the ABI, e.g. "Got a scalar pair where a scalar was expected", "invalid immediate for given destination place: value ScalarPair ... does not match ABI Scalar", or an "unknown layout" ICE.
preconditions: The impossible/trivial bound is inherited from a parent item (struct/trait/enclosing function) rather than present directly on the body's own DefId.
A later MIR pass or const-eval performs work on the body (GVN, Inline, const propagation, known-panics lint, promotion, drop elaboration).
The body contains a value whose layout/const evaluation depends on the unsatisfiable predicate, e.g. `Option<str>`, `Option<&str>`, a promoted closure allocation, or an associated const/type.
For error-bound cases, the predicate references an error type (unknown path `b`, disallowed `Self`, etc.); for const cases, the clause may contain an unevaluated const projection.
For trivial global bounds the feature gate `trivial_bounds` (or `non_lifetime_binders` for `for<T> T: Copy`) is enabled and the expected warning is allowed/expected.
pitfalls: Using `predicates_of(...).predicates` alone omits parent predicates; use `instantiate_identity(tcx)` so inherited bounds are considered.
`p.is_global()` and the new `!HAS_FREE_LOCAL_NAMES` filter are related but not literally identical; verify the flag-based filter does not admit non-global clauses.
Do not feed clauses with `HAS_CT_PROJECTION` into the impossibility check; the patch comments that unevaluated constants 'cause cycles'.
Error-referencing predicates must short-circuit (`predicates.references_error()`); otherwise error recovery can reach const evaluation and ICE.

The pass is intentionally double-edged: clearing the body degrades diagnostics to `error[E0080]: entering unreachable code` with `evaluation of ... failed here`. Existing stderr expectations for unknown layout or 'failed inside this call' change; do not treat that message change as a correctness regression.
Moving `tests/crashes/*.rs` to `tests/ui/...` and adding `//@ build-pass` is part of the regression coverage; a test that still expects the old error message will not verify the unreachable marking.
Diagnostics span shifts occur (e.g. from the inner type to the whole const expression); update test annotations accordingly.
analysis.testStrategy: Add UI regression tests where the impossible bound lives on a parent item and a descendant/derived body performs const work. For inherited trivial bounds use a derived impl or closure under `where str: Sized` / `where for<T> T: Copy`, compile with `-Zmir-enable-passes=+GVN -Zmir-enable-passes=+Inline -Zvalidate-mir --crate-type lib` and `//@ build-pass`; for error bounds use `fn a() where b: Sized` and `fn f() -> &'static str where Self: Sized` with `-C opt-level=1 -Zvalidate-mir` and expect the normal name-resolution errors but no ICE. Companion UI tests should assert the new diagnostic `error[E0080]: entering unreachable code` plus the note `evaluation of ... failed here` for cases such as `[(); { let _a: Option<str> = None; 0 }]`, `size_of::<<() as Project>::Assoc>()`, and generic-const-expr type-alias bounds.
